chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Hasan ibn Zarif, from Abdul Samad ibn Bashir, from Abu Al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Al-Jaroud, what do they say to you regarding Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them)?' I said, 'They deny us that they are the sons of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' He said, 'So by what argument do you argue against them?' I said, 'We argue against them by the Statement of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, regarding Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him): And of his descendants, Dawud and Sulaiman and Ayyub and Yusuf and Musa and Harun; and thus do We reward those who do good. And Zakariya and Yahya and Isa. So He made Isa ibn Maryam from the descendants of Noah (peace be upon him).'

He said, 'So what is it that they say to you?' I said, 'They say, 'The child of a daughter can be from the son, but he is not from the loins (seed).' He said, 'So which argument do you use against them?' I said, 'We argue against them by the Statement of Allah, the Exalted, to His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family): Say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons and our women and your women and ourselves and your selves.' He said, 'So what do they say?' I said, 'They say that in the speech of the Arabs, a man may say

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Al-Jaroud, I will give it to you from the Book of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, that they are from the loins of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). None shall reject it except the disbeliever.' I said, 'And where is that? May I be sacrificed for you.' He said, 'From where Allah, the Exalted, said: Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters and your sisters... the verse until it ends with the words of the Blessed and Exalted: And the wives of your sons who are from your loins.' So ask them, O Abu Al-Jaroud, was it permissible for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to marry the wives of the two of them? If they say, 'Yes,' they lied and were mischievous; and if they say, 'No,' then they are his sons from his loins.'

key_terms.حَلَائِلُ أَبْنَائِكُمُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ أ: Wives of your sons who are from your loins
key_terms.قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: The Statement of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty

ai.seo_question: How does the Quran prove the biological lineage of Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn from the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this dialogue with Abu al-Jarud, Imam al-Baqir (AS) employs a logical deduction from the Quranic verse of Mahram prohibitions (4:23), specifically the phrase 'wives of your sons who are from your loins' (min aslābikum), to establish the biological lineage of Hasan and Husayn. He argues that if they were merely sons by marriage (ibn al-bint) rather than by loins, the prohibition would not apply, and the Prophet could have married their wives; since the opponents deny this, the biological connection is confirmed. This hadith is pivotal in Shia scholarship for refuting the Sunni claim of 'al-ibn al-bint' (son of the daughter) and affirming the direct patrilineal descent of the Imams.
